Severe Flooding Hits Swedish Cable & Satellite Facilities, Operations Disrupted

A series of intense storms has triggered widespread flooding in southern Sweden, severely affecting the Cable & Satellite industry’s operational sites and threatening to prolong service disruptions. The persistent heavy rainfall, which began late last week, inundated ground stations and uplink centers in the Skåne and Halland regions, where several leading industry firms maintain core infrastructure.

Industry sources confirm that at least five transmission facilities operated by major firms such as NordSat AB and SkyFiber Sverige have sustained water damage, with some sites forced to evacuate non-essential staff. “The floodwaters have reached critical areas within our Ystad control center,” said Lena Andersson, spokesperson for NordSat AB. “Our technical teams are working around the clock to protect signal routing equipment and restore partial operations, but access remains difficult due to ongoing high water levels.”

According to the Swedish Cable & Satellite Workers’ Union, more than 110 workers have been temporarily relocated from sites at highest risk, and several technicians remain on standby for rapid deployments to safeguard key infrastructure. “Our priority is the safety of the workforce, but we are also focused on minimizing signal interruptions for end users,” said union chair Erik Lundström.

The Swedish Cable & Satellite Association reported that unmanned relay stations in low-lying rural areas have lost power or become inaccessible, hampering troubleshooting and routine maintenance efforts. “We are monitoring the situation closely and coordinating with local authorities to ensure we can resume normal operations as soon as conditions allow,” said association director Anna Sjöberg.

Analysts warn that if water levels do not recede within the next 48 hours, damage to fiber and satellite uplink hardware could escalate, potentially extending disruptions. The full extent of the impact will depend on how quickly emergency teams can secure affected sites and restore equipment.

As the storms persist, industry stakeholders are bracing for continued operational challenges, with further updates expected as the situation develops.
